mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of at least 0.3 percentage points in UNRATE and a fall of at least 0.5% in PAYEMS within the same month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (personal savings) of at least 2% each signals a weakening housing market and reduced household liquidity, which depresses consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > -2% AND RSAFS falls > -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL (consumer price index) rises by more than 0.4% month-over-month for three consecutive months, it signals persistent inflation, prompting expectations of tighter monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which erodes corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered quarters.
